To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the exclusion of birds and bats from the canopy of oaks leads to an increase in leaf damage, (2) the effect of exclusion on leaf damage is greater on young than mature trees and (3) leaf damage was 59% greater in the south than in the central study area.
insectivorous birds (and bats) are important predators of herbivorous insects in the crowns, and that this effect is more pronounced in young than mature trees.
insectivorous birds, bats and other vertebrates play an important role in reducing herbivore damage to leaves in the crowns (canopy) of oaks in Germany.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of vertebrate herbivore regulation in the context of forest management and conservation.
a better understanding of the role of vertebrate predation in temperate forest ecosystems.
a better understanding of the role of vertebrate insectivores in the control of herbivy and the impact of their loss on ecosystem processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
birds and bats have a significant top-down effect in controlling herbivory of oaks, which is dependent on the local conditions.
insectivorous birds, and to some extent bats, reduce the density of herbivorous insects and hence herbivory on oak leaves in the crowns.
the effects of vertebrate predators on herbivory depend on the site, the species composition and the tree age.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intensive foraging of aerial vertebrates in temperate forests is an important mechanism to reduce leaf damage by herbivorous arthopods.
the control of herbivority is more effective in the crowns than in the understory of temperate forests.
top-down control by birds and bats is important for reducing leaf damage in the canopy of broad leaved oak forests.
The main takeaway from our work is that
insectivorous vertebrate predators can have strong top down effects on leaf damage through predation of herbivorous insects in the canopy of temperate forests.
insectivorous vertebrate predators can reduce leaf damage in temperate forest canopoes by up to 50%.
the impact of insectivorous bats and birds on leaf damage is highly variable and depends on the local context.
